ambiguity_rule: BROWN_VERB_VS_COLOUR: brown the meat is FAT_HEAT (a pan step); 'cook until browned' is an endpoint cue (COLOUR) of the cooking step
REDUCE_VERB_VS_ENDPOINT: reduce the sauce is WET_HEAT (evaporation); 'simmer until reduced by half' is an endpoint cue (EVAPORATE_REDUCE) of the simmer; 'reduce the heat' is HEAT_CONTROL adjust-heat
INFUSE_HOT_VS_COLD: infuse / steep in hot liquid is WET_HEAT; a cold steep over hours is uptake (FERMENT_LEAVEN)
COOL_AMBIENT_VS_REST: cool / let cool on a rack or the counter is COOLING to ambient (environment ROOM); RESTING is only the verbs rest / stand / sit; 'a cool place' is a noun phrase, not a process
CHILL_VS_RELAX: chill the dish is COOLING; chill a dough or batter to relax or firm it is still COOLING (temperature falls); only a stated fermentation or proving time makes it FERMENT_LEAVEN

REST_AFTER_HEAT_VS_DOUGH: rest / stand / sit is RESTING (carry-over, still air) after a heat step; on a dough or batter lot with no heat before it, a rest is a relaxation or proving step (FERMENT_LEAVEN); 'let stand 10 minutes before cooking' on cut aromatics is a waiting time (RESTING, no carry-over)
TOP_ALIAS_COLLISION: trim has the alias top ('top and tail'); PROC-000094 top is COMBINATION ('top with cheese')
PROCESS_BLEND_VS_CANNING: the alias process (food processor) is MECHANICAL_MIX blend; 'process the jars in a boiling water bath' is PRESERVATION canning (jar, canner or water-bath cue)
SQUEEZE_WATER_VS_JUICE: squeeze out the water is SEPARATION; squeeze / juice a lemon produces an ingredient lot (composition only)
TOP_ALIAS_COLLISION: see PROC-000052
BASTE_ALIAS_COLLISION: brush (COMBINATION) has the alias baste; PROC-000152 baste is FAT_HEAT; the primary family is per PROC id, the verb in text needs a heat or pan context to be FAT_HEAT
MARINATE_ACID_LONG: marinate is FERMENT_LEAVEN; an acid or salt marinade held for days is closer to PRESERVATION; the noun marinade is not a process (NON_VERB_SURFACES)
SET_PUT_VS_SET_FIRM: 'set aside', 'set the pan on the hob' is TRANSFER (put alias set); 'until set', 'leave to set' is the ENDPOINT PROC-000146 (set / firm)
STORE_PHYSICAL_VS_TRANSFER: the ledger family of store is TRANSFER; the physical family is STORAGE when a time or a storage temperature class is stated, else it is lot location only
family_override_note: ledger family TRANSFER; physical family STORAGE (nonheat_binding.nh_family)

ambiguity_rule: SOAK_DISCARD: soak is FERMENT_LEAVEN (uptake); when the soaking liquid is drained, strained or discarded in the next physical step (follows_soak_or_brine) the step pair is also a SEPARATION leaching hand-off
CURE_SALT_UPTAKE_VS_PICKLE: pickle is PRESERVATION; the alias cure (salt cure of meat or fish) is salt uptake, also FERMENT_LEAVEN
STERILISE_JARS_VS_CANNING: sterilise jars is a conditions-only step; the canning step is the process in a pressure canner (F0 scope, S177); sterilise as a word on a utensil is not food physics
CAN_MODAL_VS_VERB: 'can' is the verb (PRESERVATION) only with jars, a canner or a water bath; the modal 'can' and the noun 'can' (tin) are not processes (NON_VERB_SURFACES)

DRY_PROCESS_VS_WORD: dry / dehydrate is PRESERVATION only with a drying medium (oven, dehydrator, sun, air) or a duration of an hour or more; 'pat dry', 'wipe dry' and 'dry ingredients' are not drying (SEPARATION pat-dry or no process); 'dry-fry' is FAT_HEAT
KEEP_RESERVE_VS_STORE: reserve / save / keep for later is RESERVATION (lot bookkeeping); 'keep in the fridge for 3 days' is STORAGE (store)
REDUCE_HEAT_VS_REDUCE: lower / increase the heat is HEAT_CONTROL; the verb reduce is PROC-000028
SET_FIRM_VS_PUT: see PROC-000102; an ENDPOINT word is never an input
RISE_ENDPOINT_VS_PROVE: puff / rise as an oven state ('until risen') is ENDPOINT; 'let the dough rise' is a proving step (FERMENT_LEAVEN prove)
BASTE_ALIAS_COLLISION: see PROC-000096

BRINE_SHORT_VS_LONG: brine is PRESERVATION by default (long, days, with vinegar or pickling context); a short brine of meat or poultry (hours, salt solution, then cooked) is FERMENT_LEAVEN uptake; the noun brine in 'bring the brine to a boil' is not a process
